mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved steadily from -32.3% to -23.9% over four weeks, signaling restoration of commuting infrastructure. This trend will continue, enabling higher retail footfall as workers return to offices and pass through retail districts during commutes.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 8.4 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines by more than 5 percentage points in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has recovered from -9.4% to -5.1%, indicating reduced pandemic-driven caution and normalization of shopping behavior. This behavioral shift extends to discretionary retail, driving RETAIL_REC upward as consumers resume non-essential shopping patterns.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -6.0% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 4.3 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below -7.0% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not show positive correlation with GROCERY_PHARM improvements.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized near baseline (4.6% at t-0w after -2.1% at t-1w), indicating outdoor activity normalization. When PARKS and RETAIL_REC both improve together, it reflects broader social reopening that sustains retail demand over the four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered from -2.1% to 4.6% in one week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below -5.0% in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC and PARKS do not move in the same direction for at least two of the four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains severely depressed at -28.6%, indicating persistent remote work or capacity restrictions. If WORKPLACES does not recover above -20% within two weeks, retail will remain suppressed as office-based foot traffic and lunch-hour shopping remain constrained.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -25% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -20% in either of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points despite WORKPLACES remaining below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 7.6% to 4.7%, indicating people are spending less time at home and more time outside. This behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity will drive retail mobility upward as consumers engage in discretionary shopping and recreation.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 6.0% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a RESIDENTIAL decline below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility interact: when TRANSIT improves while WORKPLACES remains depressed, it indicates selective commuting for essential activities. This creates a bottleneck where retail benefits from transit users but lacks the office-worker base to sustain growth, resulting in flat or declining RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by >5 points while WORKPLACES remains below -25%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 8.4 points while WORKPLACES improved only 7.1 points
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -20% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points despite the TRANSIT-WORKPLACES divergence.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September marks the transition into fall retail season. GROCERY_PHARM recovery to -5.1% signals consumer confidence normalization. If this confidence persists and PARKS remains positive, seasonal back-to-school and early holiday shopping will drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above -6.0% AND PARKS above 0% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both series show positive trend at t-0w
failure_condition: Either GROCERY_PHARM falls below -8.0% or PARKS falls below -3.0% in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -25.4% with minimal week-to-week volatility (range: -26.0% to -24.9% over three weeks). This stability indicates a structural equilibrium where suppressed retail demand is locked in by persistent workplace and transit constraints, and will persist over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC variance <1.1 percentage points over last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks, or the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks exceeds -23.0%.
